brief.title: v0.2.11: GitHub Copilot through your gateway
brief.why: v0.2.10 and v0.2.11 shipped on 3 October and haven't had a post (yesterday was a take and a design-partner call), so a release beats Sunday's take. The last release post (v0.2.6, 2 Oct) was about the laptops rollout; this one leads with something any developer can try with five environment variables: Copilot CLI and VS Code's chat on your own gateway, with refusals and held requests told in the reply instead of an auth error.

cards.headline: Point Copilot at *your* gateway
cards.code:
export COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
export COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000
export COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY=ct_sk_…
export COPILOT_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-5
export COPILOT_OFFLINE=true

linkedin.text:
Your gateway blocked a request. Your developer saw "Authentication failed". Who files the ticket?

That's what we found recording real clients through Control Tower. Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Codex read a 403 as a bad sign-in, so a gate's "no" looked like a broken key. Copilot CLI showed it as "Authentication failed with provider".

Control Tower v0.2.11 is out. GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code's chat (Copilot Chat) can now use Control Tower's models, without a GitHub account for those models. Five environment variables for the CLI, a Custom Endpoint in VS Code. Every call is then on the map under its key, counted in the Ledger, and subject to your gates. Both take Control Tower's /mcp endpoint too, so your tool servers come with the same rules.

And Control Tower recognises these as a person's apps. A blocked message says which gate and why. A held one says "waiting for approval" in the reply and stays open; once approved, the answer follows in the same reply.

Both are run for real each week: Copilot CLI 1.0.91 on Windows and macOS, VS Code 1.140 with Copilot Chat 0.68.

Open source, self-hosted, one docker run: https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

A ⭐ helps others find it.

#AIAgents #DeveloperTools #OpenSource

posts:
Control Tower v0.2.11: GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code's chat can run on your own gateway's models.

No GitHub account needed for them. Five env vars for the CLI, a Custom Endpoint in VS Code. Every call on the map, in the Ledger, behind your gates.

The part I like most: a gate's "no" used to show up in Copilot CLI as "Authentication failed with provider".

Now it says which gate and why. A held request says "waiting for approval" in the reply, then the answer follows once someone approves.

Self-hosted, open source, one docker run. Tested for real against both clients every week.

A star helps others find it ⭐ https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

brief.notes: All claims from docs/changelog.md (0.2.10, 0.2.11) and docs/client-copilot.md. 'No GitHub account' applies to the models added through Control Tower; Copilot's own GitHub-hosted models, inline completions and other GitHub features still use GitHub (the doc's 'What stays with GitHub'), so the copy scopes it to 'those models'. Held-request wording in the reply is on the Messages API, which the code card uses. The 'Authentication failed with provider' quote is from the changelog. The Laptops rollout of Copilot CLI is Enterprise and isn't mentioned. Release follows the 2 Oct release post within three days because two releases shipped since with no post. Cards only: no recorder scene covers Copilot.
